entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10171"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 27</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Jer.27.1-Jer.27.22">Jr 27:1-22</reference>. The Futility of Resisting Nebuchadnezzar Illustrated to the Ambassadors of the Kings, Desiring to Have the King of Judah Confederate with Them, under the Type of Yokes. Jeremiah Exhorts Them and Zedekiah to Yield.</title> <div sID="gen18147" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10171"/><hi type="bold">1. Jehoiakim--</hi>The prophecy that follows was according to this reading given in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, fifteen years before it was published in the reign of Zedekiah to whom it refers; it was thus long deposited in the prophet's bosom, in order that by it he might be supported under trials in his prophetic career in the interim [Calvin]. But "Zedekiah" may be the true reading. So the Syriac and Arabic Versions. <reference osisRef="Jer.27.3">Jr 27:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.27.12">12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.28.1">Jr 28:1</reference>, confirm this; also, one of Kennicott's manuscripts. The English Version reading may have originated from <reference osisRef="Jer.26.1">Jr 26:1</reference>. "Son of Josiah" applies to Zedekiah as truly as to "Jehoiakim" or "Eliakim." The fourth year may, in a general sense here, as in <reference osisRef="Jer.28.1">Jr 28:1</reference>, be called "the beginning of his reign," as it lasted eleven years (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.24.18">2Ki 24:18</reference>). It was not long after the fourth year of his reign that he rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar (<reference osisRef="Jer.51.59">Jr 51:59</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.52.3">52:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.24.20">2Ki 24:20</reference>), in violation of an oath before God (<reference osisRef="2Chr.36.13">2Ch 36:13</reference>). <div eID="gen18147" type="x-p"/>

The Futility of Resisting Nebuchadnezzar Illustrated to the Ambassadors of the Kings, Desiring to Have the King of Judah Confederate with Them, under the Type of Yokes. Jehoiakim-- The prophecy that follows was according to this reading given in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, fifteen years before it was published in the reign of Zedekiah to whom it refers; it was thus long deposited in the prophet's bosom, in order that by it he might be supported under trials in his prophetic career in the interim [Calvin]. But "Zedekiah" may be the true reading. So the Syriac and Arabic Versions. Jr 27:3 , 12 ; Jr 28:1 , confirm this; also, one of Kennicott's manuscripts. The English Version reading may have originated from Jr 26:1 . "Son of Josiah" applies to Zedekiah as truly as to "Jehoiakim" or "Eliakim." The fourth year may, in a general sense here, as in Jr 28:1 , be called "the beginning of his reign," as it lasted eleven years ( 2Ki 24:18 ). It was not long after the fourth year of his reign that he rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar ( Jr 51:59 ; 52:3 ; 2Ki 24:20 ), in violation of an oath before God ( 2Ch 36:13 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10173"/><div sID="gen18150" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10173"/><hi type="bold">3. And send them to the king of Edom, &c.--</hi>Appropriate symbol, as these ambassadors had come to Jerusalem to consult as to shaking off the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar. According to Pherecydes in Clement of Alexandria [Miscellanies, 567], Idanthura, king of the Scythians, intimated to Darius, who had crossed the Danube, that he would lead an army against him, by sending him, instead of a letter, a mouse, a frog, a bird, an arrow, and a plough. The task assigned to Jeremiah required great faith, as it was sure to provoke alike his own countrymen and the foreign ambassadors and their kings, by a seeming insult, at the very time that all were full of confident hopes grounded on the confederacy. <div eID="gen18150" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10175"/><div sID="gen18153" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10175"/><hi type="bold">6. beasts of the field--</hi>not merely the horses to carry his Chaldean soldiers, and oxen to draw his provisions [Grotius]; not merely the deserts, mountains, and woods, the haunts of wild beasts, implying his unlimited extent of empire [Estius]; but the beasts themselves by a mysterious instinct of nature. A reproof to men that they did not recognize God's will, which the very beasts acknowledged (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.1.3">Is 1:3</reference>). As the beasts are to submit to Christ, the Restorer of the dominion over nature, lost by the first Adam (compare <reference osisRef="Gen.1.28">Ge 1:28</reference>; 2:19, 20; <reference osisRef="Ps.8.6-Ps.8.8">Psa 8:6-8</reference>), so they were appointed to submit to Nebuchadnezzar, the representative of the world power and prefigurer of Antichrist; this universal power was suffered to be held by him to show the unfitness of any to wield it "until He come whose right it is" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.21.27">Eze 21:27</reference>). <div eID="gen18153" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10176"/><div sID="gen18154" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10176"/><hi type="bold">7. son ... son's son--</hi>(<reference osisRef="2Chr.36.20">2Ch 36:20</reference>). Nebuchadnezzar had four successors--Evil-merodach, his son; Neriglissar, husband of Nebuchadnezzar's daughter; his son, Labosodarchod; and Naboned (with whom his son, Belshazzar, was joint king), son of Evil-merodach. But Neriglissar and Labosodarchod were not in the direct male line; so that the prophecy held good to "his son and his son's son," and the intermediate two are omitted.<div eID="gen18154" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18155" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">time of his land--</hi>that is, of its subjugation or its being "visited" in wrath (<reference osisRef="Jer.27.22">Jr 27:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.25.12">Jr 25:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.29.10">29:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.50.27">50:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.5.26">Da 5:26</reference>).<div eID="gen18155" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18156" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">serve themselves of him--</hi>make him their servant (<reference osisRef="Jer.25.14">Jr 25:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.13.22">Is 13:22</reference>). So "his day" for the destined day of his calamity (<reference osisRef="Job.18.20">Job 18:20</reference>). <div eID="gen18156" type="x-p"/>
